_about: Drawn 3D board for site/boardviz (tools/boardviz/README.md). Millimeters from the board's bottom-left corner, x right, y up, rot in degrees counterclockwise. parts: the hand-placed parts, each with a type the part library knows; a part with an id can carry a label and text shown when tapped. headers: cols x rows at 2.54 mm, pins named top row first, left column first; pins with names become tap targets. decor: two-pad parts found by tools/boardviz/pads_from_drawing.py, drawn but never labelled.
source: Positions read from the top-side PCB layout and the board picture in the kit's user guide (SLVUE03, figures 2-1, 2-4 and 5-4), scale set from the 2.54 mm header pitch. Checked 2026-11-09 against the guide's board photo (figure 2-1): shield can, probe plug, LEDs and buttons placed from it.

parts.label: The chip
parts.title: CC2755P10
parts.text: A 96 MHz Arm Cortex-M33 with 1,024 kB of flash and 162 kB of RAM, and a 2.4 GHz radio for Bluetooth LE, Zigbee, Thread and Matter. 40-pin VQFN.

parts.label: Antenna
parts.title: Printed antenna
parts.text: The long copper trace along the bottom edge is the 2.4 GHz antenna. Keep metal and your hand away from it when you measure range.

parts.label: U.FL
parts.title: Antenna test socket
parts.text: A tiny coax socket for connecting a cable to a spectrum analyzer or an outside antenna instead of the printed one.

parts.name: LED red
parts.label: Red LED
parts.title: Red LED on DIO16
parts.text: A user LED on DIO16. Jumper P2 pins 1 and 2 connect it; pull the jumper to use DIO16 on header pin J4:36.

parts.name: LED green
parts.label: Green LED
parts.title: Green LED on DIO12
parts.text: A user LED on DIO12. Jumper P2 pins 2 and 4 connect it; pull the jumper to use DIO12 on header pin J2:19.

parts.label: LED jumper
parts.title: P2, LED enable
parts.text: Two small jumper spots that join the red and green LEDs to their chip pins. Remove one to free that pin on the BoosterPack header.

parts.label: BTN-1
parts.title: BTN-1 on DIO20
parts.text: A user button on DIO20, also wired to header pin J3:30.

parts.label: BTN-2
parts.title: BTN-2 on DIO0
parts.text: A user button on DIO0, also wired to header pin J4:40.

parts.label: 10-pin debug
parts.title: P4, Arm 10-pin debug
parts.text: A standard 10-pin debug header. An outside probe can program and debug the chip here instead of the plug on the top edge.

parts.label: Debug plug
parts.title: P3, probe connector
parts.text: The 20-pin plug on the top edge. It goes into an LP-XDS110ET or LP-XDS110, which powers the board and gives it SWD, a serial port and reset.

parts.label: J1
parts.title: BoosterPack J1
parts.text: Outer left column, pins 1 to 10 from the top: 3V3 and chip pins. Plug-on boards stack here.

parts.label: J3
parts.title: BoosterPack J3
parts.text: Inner left column, pins 21 to 30: 5 V, ground, then the I2S and analog pins.

parts.label: J4
parts.title: BoosterPack J4
parts.text: Inner right column, pins 40 down to 31: DIO0 at the top, the LED and SWD pins, then DIO18.

parts.label: J2
parts.title: BoosterPack J2
parts.text: Outer right column, pins 20 down to 11: ground, the SPI pins and the launchpad reset.

parts.label: 5V and ground
parts.title: P5, 5 V and ground
parts.text: Three holes for a wire or pin: ground and 5 V.

parts.label: 3V3 and ground
parts.title: P1, 3.3 V and ground
parts.text: Three holes for a wire or pin: ground and 3.3 V. Use them to power the board without the debugger.

parts.label: RF shield
parts.title: Shield can
parts.text: A metal can over the radio chip and its crystals. Its round holes let the board's reflow heat out.
